claims.claim: A user journey is a scenario-based sequence of the steps a person takes to accomplish a high-level goal with a company or product, usually across channels and over time.

A journey map is a visualization of the process a person goes through to accomplish a goal; its key elements are an actor, a scenario, journey phases, and the actions, mindsets, and emotions within each phase.
A touchpoint is a time when the actor in the map actually interacts with the company, while a channel is a method of communication or service delivery, such as the website or a physical store.
Journey maps help teams highlight areas of friction and pain points across the whole experience, including gaps where no internal team owns part of the journey.
A user journey is macro and holistic while a user flow is micro: a set of interactions describing the steps needed to accomplish one common task within a product.
The heart of a journey map's narrative is what the user is doing, thinking, and feeling during the journey, and those data points should be based on qualitative research.

Journey maps are research-based tools that condense and simplify complex experiences into a shared picture; they are models for communication and design, not exact records of any single person's experience.

conflictingEvidence.issue: IxDF states that a customer journey map is 'often synonymous with a user flow diagram,' while NN/g draws a firm distinction between journeys (macro, holistic) and user flows (micro, task-specific). This lesson follows the NN/g distinction and treats user flows as a sibling topic, as the subject source-map requires.

sourceRecords.title: Journey Mapping 101
sourceRecords.notes: Read live via HTTP with a browser user agent on 2026-08-21 (article by Sarah Gibbons, December 9, 2018, last reviewed July 15, 2026). Supports: the definition of a journey map as a visualization of the process a person goes through to accomplish a goal; the five key components (actor, scenario and expectations, journey phases, actions/mindsets/emotions, opportunities); the interchangeability of 'user journey map' and 'customer journey map'; pain-point discovery; journey maps being best for sequences of events and multi-channel scenarios. Facts restated in original prose.

sourceRecords.title: User Journeys vs. User Flows
sourceRecords.notes: Read live via HTTP with a browser user agent on 2026-08-21 (article by Kate Kaplan, April 16, 2023). Supports the working definitions: a user journey is a scenario-based sequence of steps to accomplish a high-level goal, usually across channels and over time; a user flow is a set of interactions for one common task within a product; and the macro (journey) vs micro (flow) distinction. Facts restated in original prose.

sourceRecords.title: When and How to Create Customer Journey Maps
